title: Third Reich Sites in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin did not keep the buildings of the perpetrators, so most of these sites are ground rather than architecture.** A car park, a gravel field, a square, a plate of glass in the paving. Two things decide whether a place is worth your afternoon: how much of the original is physically there, and whether anything on site explains it.

**Start at the Topography of Terror.** Free, daily 10:00 to 20:00, on the excavated cellars of the Gestapo and SS headquarters, with 200 metres of the Berlin Wall above them. It is the only place that lays out how the institutions fitted together, and everything else assumes you already know that.

**The biggest surviving Nazi building in central Berlin is a working government ministry.** The 1935 to 1936 Reich Aviation Ministry at Wilhelmstraße 97 is intact and now the Federal Ministry of Finance. Exterior only, and worth ten minutes for the 1953 mural and the 17 June memorial sunk into the pavement in front of it.
**The Führerbunker really is nothing.** A car park on In den Ministergärten with one information board, put up on 8 June 2006. Four minutes if you are already walking past, and not worth a detour.

**Nine of the eleven sites are free to walk into.** Topography of Terror, the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe with the Information Centre under it, Bebelplatz, the bunker car park, the old Aviation Ministry from the pavement, the German Resistance Memorial Center, Gleis 17, the House of the Wannsee Conference and Sachsenhausen. Only Olympiastadion (€11 self-guided) and the Tempelhof building tour charge, and the Tempelhof airfield itself is a free public park.

**Two of them need a real block of time.** Wannsee is S1 or S7 plus bus 114, about 45 minutes each way in zone AB. Sachsenhausen is a half day minimum, zones ABC. Do not stack either of them on top of a full central day.
